title: Celebrating Bhai Dooj: A Festival of Sibling Bonding
excerpt: Bhai Dooj honors the special bond between brothers and sisters.
body:
Bhai Dooj, celebrated on the second day after Diwali, is a significant festival in India that symbolizes the love and bond between brothers and sisters. It is a day when sisters pray for their brothers' long life and prosperity, while brothers express their gratitude and promise to protect their sisters.

The festival is marked by various rituals. Sisters typically apply a ceremonial tilak (a mark) on their brothers' foreheads and perform aarti, followed by offering sweets and gifts. Brothers, in turn, give gifts to their sisters as a token of appreciation. Traditional foods like sweets, snacks, and festive meals are prepared, making it a joyous occasion for families.

For many diaspora families, Bhai Dooj serves as a cherished opportunity to reconnect with cultural roots. Families often gather for a special meal, share memories, and exchange gifts, even if they are miles apart. Virtual celebrations have become common, allowing siblings to participate in rituals together through video calls, ensuring that the spirit of the festival remains alive, no matter the distance.
